editorial_review_row.author: NAFT Editorial
editorial_review_row.content: Octa holds a legitimate CySEC licence (372/18) and offers genuinely low-cost trading from 0.6 pips with zero commission — but in 2026 the broker is engulfed in a regulatory crisis after its founder was named in an Rs 800 crore Indian Enforcement Directorate money laundering case, subsequently had his voting rights stripped by CySEC, and has been arrested. Most global clients are routed to an offshore MISA entity in Saint Lucia with no investor compensation scheme. The trading product works. The question is whether you trust the organisation behind it while enforcement agencies in multiple countries are actively investigating its leadership.
